author: WP13
summary: Updated chapter on the Model/ModelMesh/ModelMeshPart runtime: draw contract, part/effect bookkeeping, thread-local scratch, model content routes, copy and ownership semantics, hand-built graphs, the root-bone constructor and collection rules. Largely current, but several claims are stale at TARGET: Draw throws InvalidOperationException, a concurrency test exists, empty names throw ArgumentNullException, the CNJ route computes bounding spheres, XNB keeps tags and uses the root-index constructor, a fifth (.cnb) route exists and copy/unload behaviour is test-pinned. The site had the user-level API and examples; the contract depth now lives on the model runtime and skinning deep dives.

concepts.section: Models, Meshes, and Drawing
concepts.text: The Model runtime is the XNA-shaped graph Model -> ModelMesh -> ModelMeshPart plus bones; at runtime the important distinction is a reader-built, internally consistent graph versus a hand-built one.
tokens: reader-built, internally consistent graph or a hand-built one

concepts.section: Models, Meshes, and Drawing
concepts.text: Model API parity with FNA is described by named, intentional C++ safety deviations (copy loop bound, null-effect skip, null parent as bone 0, checked indexers) rather than by a blanket zero-gap claim.
tokens: null-effect skip is a CNA deviation

concepts.section: The runtime hierarchy
concepts.text: Model holds a ModelBoneCollection and a ModelMeshCollection; each ModelMesh holds a ModelMeshPartCollection and a derived ModelEffectCollection; each part points at a VertexBuffer, IndexBuffer and Effect, the same shape as XNA.

concepts.section: The runtime hierarchy
concepts.text: Every link of the graph is a non-owning raw pointer: parts store raw buffer/effect/Tag addresses, meshes raw part and device addresses, bones raw parent/child addresses, the model vectors of raw bone and mesh pointers.

concepts.section: The runtime hierarchy
concepts.text: A loaded graph is kept alive by one private std::shared_ptr<void> ownedResources_ set through the CNAEXT setOwnedResources hook; every reader allocates the whole graph into one bundle.

concepts.section: The runtime hierarchy
concepts.text: CNA makes public several members FNA keeps internal to its reader: the CNAEXT Model constructors, ModelBone(int, name) and AddChild, the ModelMesh constructors, and the read-write BoundingSphere and ParentBone setters.

concepts.section: The runtime hierarchy
concepts.text: ModelMeshPart has CNAEXT mutators SetVertexBuffer, SetIndexBuffer, SetVertexOffset, SetNumVertices, SetStartIndex and SetPrimitiveCount because XNA's own setters are content-pipeline-only.

concepts.section: The runtime hierarchy
concepts.text: Those public setters turn reader-populated metadata into caller-maintained state, which is why the draw contract's invariants matter for hand-built graphs.

concepts.section: The runtime hierarchy
concepts.text: CopyAbsoluteBoneTransformsTo, CopyBoneTransformsFrom and CopyBoneTransformsTo throw ArgumentOutOfRangeException for a shorter vector and otherwise loop over Bones.Count, leaving extra destination elements untouched.

concepts.section: The runtime hierarchy
concepts.text: The Bones.Count loop bound is a deliberate deviation from FNA, whose loop bound is the destination array length; it is never a compatibility problem for correctly sized callers.
tokens: loop bound is the destination array length

concepts.section: The runtime hierarchy
concepts.text: Model::Draw is a convenience that binds World/View/Projection through IEffectMatrices on the mesh effects and draws every mesh.

concepts.section: Two ways to draw a loaded model
concepts.text: The one-call model.Draw(world, view, projection) is correct for any loaded, renderable model with at least a root bone, even without an interesting hierarchy.

concepts.section: Two ways to draw a loaded model
concepts.text: A multi-bone model can be drawn by hand: CopyAbsoluteBoneTransformsTo into a bone-count vector, compose each mesh's parent-bone absolute transform with world, set the effect matrices, then ModelMesh::Draw.

concepts.section: Two ways to draw a loaded model
concepts.text: The manual loop should set matrices through IEffectMatrices: glTF and converted .cnj models carry PbrEffect/SkinnedPbrEffect for metallic-roughness materials, so a dynamic_cast<BasicEffect*> loop silently skips them.
concepts.note: Extended at TARGET: the effect a glTF part gets is PBR for every non-unlit material, so the BasicEffect-cast pattern on the site misses such parts.

concepts.section: Two ways to draw a loaded model
concepts.text: The bone index selects the mesh's parent-bone absolute transform, not bone 0 and not the model root.
tokens: not bone 0 and not the model root

concepts.section: Two ways to draw a loaded model
concepts.text: An earlier loose-JSON route assigned one default bone to every mesh and welded independently placed parts together.
concepts.note: Positive evidence: the .cnj reader attaches each mesh to its serialized parentBone (version 2) or to its own named child bone of Root (version 1) in ContentManager.cpp ModelTypeReader::Read (hasBoneHierarchy branch); the page keeps it only as history.

concepts.section: Two ways to draw a loaded model
concepts.text: The per-mesh parent-bone pattern applies to XNB, .cnj and direct glTF outputs; skinned meshes are the exception because they hang off bone 0 and are placed by their palette.
concepts.note: Adds the skinned-mesh exception that TARGET's glTF loader implements.

concepts.section: The draw contract: a model is more than a bag of pointers
concepts.text: Model::Draw is a thin convenience path, not a validator or a general scene graph.

concepts.section: The draw contract: a model is more than a bag of pointers
concepts.text: Model::Draw keeps a static thread_local scratch vector sharedDrawBoneMatrices_ that grows only when a later model on that thread has more bones and never shrinks.

concepts.section: The draw contract: a model is more than a bag of pointers
concepts.text: Model::Draw fills the scratch vector with CopyAbsoluteBoneTransformsTo and then visits every mesh.

concepts.section: The draw contract: a model is more than a bag of pointers
concepts.text: An effect in a mesh's effect collection that does not implement IEffectMatrices makes Model::Draw throw System::InvalidOperationException; it is not skipped or drawn with another convention.
concepts.note: The claim said std::runtime_error; TARGET throws the XNA exception System::InvalidOperationException, pinned by a unit test.

concepts.section: The draw contract: a model is more than a bag of pointers
concepts.text: For each effect Model::Draw writes World = boneAbsolute[parentIndex] * world, then View and Projection, and only then calls ModelMesh::Draw.

concepts.section: The draw contract: a model is more than a bag of pointers
concepts.text: Model::Draw never installs a skin palette; SetBoneTransforms on skinned effects is the application's job.
tokens: It never installs a skin palette

concepts.section: The draw contract: a model is more than a bag of pointers
concepts.text: A null ParentBone is treated as bone index 0 in Model::Draw, whereas FNA dereferences the mesh parent; this helps one-root hand-built models.
tokens: using bone index 0 when the mesh's ParentBone is null

concepts.section: The draw contract: a model is more than a bag of pointers
concepts.text: A zero-bone model with an effect is not drawable: index 0 is read from a scratch vector the model never grew (empty on a fresh thread, or a stale slot left by an earlier larger model) with unchecked operator[].

concepts.section: The draw contract: a model is more than a bag of pointers
concepts.text: CopyAbsoluteBoneTransformsTo composes in a single forward pass and requires parent-before-child storage; it neither sorts nor detects cycles, duplicate parents or index/position disagreement.
tokens: Bones must be stored parent before child

concepts.section: The draw contract: a model is more than a bag of pointers
concepts.text: A manual draw loop that dereferences the mesh parent has no null fallback; loaders assign parents, except that the XNB reader leaves ParentBone null for a null serialized parent reference.
tokens: The manual loop has no fallback
concepts.note: TARGET: the XNB reader maps a -1 (null) serialized parent to a null ParentBone; the claim's 'shared-resource reference of zero' wording is replaced by that.

concepts.section: The draw contract: a model is more than a bag of pointers
concepts.text: ModelMesh::Draw calls the renderer's Ensure3DSupported only when the mesh has a device; the shared default is a no-op and among current identities only DIRECT2D, HTML_DOM and SVG_DOM override it.

concepts.section: The draw contract: a model is more than a bag of pointers
concepts.text: ModelMesh::Draw skips a part whose Effect is null or whose PrimitiveCount is not positive; per CNA's comments FNA skips only the count case and then dereferences a null effect.

concepts.section: The draw contract: a model is more than a bag of pointers
concepts.text: For every pass of the part effect's current technique ModelMesh::Draw calls Apply and DrawIndexedPrimitives with the part's own CNAEXT primitive type, vertex offset, vertex count, start index and primitive count.
concepts.note: TARGET draws each part with its own topology (GLTF-073); non-glTF parts default to TriangleList.

concepts.section: The draw contract: a model is more than a bag of pointers
concepts.text: No part field other than effect and count is validated: raw buffers, offsets and counts go straight to GraphicsDevice, so construction success does not prove a model is drawable.
tokens: successfully constructed model is therefore not proof that it is drawable

concepts.section: The draw contract: a model is more than a bag of pointers
concepts.text: Ensure3DSupported is guarded by a null-device check but the subsequent device calls are not, so a positive-count part in a mesh built with a null device dereferences null.
tokens: built with a null device dereferences null

concepts.section: Keep parts and effects connected through the part setter
concepts.text: ModelMesh::Effects is a derived, distinct-effect view of the effects used by its parts; Model::Draw configures it before ModelMesh::Draw applies each part's technique.

concepts.section: Keep parts and effects connected through the part setter
concepts.text: The supported way to maintain Effects is ModelMeshPart::setEffectProperty: a new non-null effect is added if absent and the old one is removed only when no sibling part still uses it.

concepts.section: Keep parts and effects connected through the part setter
concepts.text: setEffectProperty is a no-op for the same pointer and scans the sibling parts (an O(parts) check, not a reference count) before removing an old effect.

concepts.section: Keep parts and effects connected through the part setter
concepts.text: Two parts sharing one BasicEffect produce one matrix setup in Model::Draw but two indexed draws.

concepts.section: Keep parts and effects connected through the part setter
concepts.text: The part/effect unit tests cover retain-on-shared, release-on-last-user and the no-duplicate case.

concepts.section: Keep parts and effects connected through the part setter
concepts.text: A part learns its owning mesh only when the ModelMesh constructor adopts it; setEffectProperty on an orphan part just stores the pointer, so its effect never reaches Effects. CNA's readers therefore attach effects after constructing the mesh.

concepts.section: Keep parts and effects connected through the part setter
concepts.text: Material-variant switching sets the part effect last, after vertex buffer, vertex count, tag and samplers, so an observer finding the effect via Effects sees complete part state.

concepts.section: Keep parts and effects connected through the part setter
concepts.text: ModelEffectCollection::Add/Remove and ModelMesh::getEffectsPropertyMutable are CNAEXT escape hatches that exist to make CNA's readers possible, unlike FNA's internal-only mutation.

concepts.section: Keep parts and effects connected through the part setter
concepts.text: Add does not deduplicate and Remove removes only the first match; neither repairs an inconsistent collection, so a stale extra effect is configured but never applied and a duplicate is configured twice.

concepts.section: Keep parts and effects connected through the part setter
concepts.text: Game code should not populate Effects directly; set each part's effect and keep buffers and effects alive as long as the model uses their raw pointers.

concepts.section: Thread-local scratch and evidence boundary
concepts.text: The draw scratch vector is thread_local: FNA shares one static array per process, and CNA's header explains that one buffer per thread is observably identical for single-threaded code while removing a resize/use-after-free race.

concepts.section: Thread-local scratch and evidence boundary
concepts.text: A unit test runs four threads drawing 2-bone and 150-bone models 400 times each and checks each effect received its own thread's transform; its parts have zero primitive count so only matrix binding runs.
concepts.note: The claim said no located test covers concurrent Draw; TARGET has this test.

concepts.section: Thread-local scratch and evidence boundary
concepts.text: thread_local scratch does not make the device, effects, buffers or a shared mutable model graph thread-safe; keep a model's update and draw on the device's thread.

concepts.section: Thread-local scratch and evidence boundary
concepts.text: ModelTests (24 cases) cover transform composition, destination-size checks, the four/five-argument constructors, whole-model bounds, the IEffectMatrices refusal and concurrency; part and collection suites cover bookkeeping.
concepts.note: TARGET's suite is broader than the claim listed (adds Draw refusal, concurrency and bounding-sphere cases).

concepts.section: Thread-local scratch and evidence boundary
concepts.text: Pixel-level drawing of Model graphs is exercised by EasyGL example programs (model draw, child-mesh hierarchy, two meshes with effects) and an SDL_Renderer program proves a populated model reaches the 2D renderer's refusal; other GPU families draw models only via glTF L7 campaigns.
concepts.note: The claim that current GPU families have equivalent two-mesh/hierarchy tests is not supported: only EasyGL has renderer-local model programs.

concepts.section: Thread-local scratch and evidence boundary
concepts.text: No located test deliberately covers zero-bone draws, invalid parent order or cycles, out-of-range part fields or a desynchronised Effects collection; treat them as construction-time invariants.

concepts.section: Four model asset routes, not two
concepts.text: Model loading has more than the old two loaders: at TARGET five content routes produce a model type — .xnb, .cnb, self-contained .cnj, direct .gltf/.glb, and the legacy .skinnedmodel.json route that returns SkinnedModelEXT.
tokens: Five content routes that produce a model
concepts.note: Four routes in the claim; TARGET adds the compiled .cnb route (schema 1 and 2).

concepts.section: Four model asset routes, not two
concepts.text: Load<Model> resolves after the cache: name.xnb, name.cnb, a literal .cnb name, the literal name, name.cnj, then name.gltf and name.glb; an .xnb hides everything and a .cnb hides its loose sources.
concepts.note: The claim's order lacked the .cnb tiers that TARGET inserts after .xnb.

concepts.section: Four model asset routes, not two
concepts.text: A same-named .cnj hides a .gltf/.glb, and passing an existing literal name.gltf reaches that literal before the extensionless .cnj probe.

concepts.section: Four model asset routes, not two
concepts.text: The XNB ModelReader is wire-compatible with XNA/MonoGame/FNA compiled models: it rebuilds the serialized bone hierarchy, each mesh's serialized parent, the serialized BoundingSphere and shared VertexBuffer/IndexBuffer/Effect resources.

concepts.section: Four model asset routes, not two
concepts.text: The XNB reader passes the file's serialized root index to the five-argument Model constructor.

concepts.section: Four model asset routes, not two
concepts.text: XNB model, mesh and part Tags are retained when they deserialize as std::shared_ptr<System::Object> or a string-keyed dictionary (boxed into ObjectDictionaryEXT); other non-null shapes are refused.
concepts.note: The claim said XNB rejects non-null Tags; TARGET keeps object and dictionary tags in its ownership bundle.

concepts.section: Four model asset routes, not two
concepts.text: The .cnj ModelTypeReader validates a Model envelope and rejects sourceFile; the .model.json name survives only in comments and test-target names, not in the reader's extension list (.cnj, .gltf, .glb).

concepts.section: Four model asset routes, not two
concepts.text: A version-2 .cnj rebuilds its parent-before-child bones array and attaches each mesh to its parentBone; a version-1 descriptor gets one Root plus a synthetic child bone per mesh.

concepts.section: Four model asset routes, not two
concepts.text: An optional skeleton/animations pair in a .cnj builds SkinningData on Model::Tag and morph data lives on the part Tag.

concepts.section: Four model asset routes, not two
concepts.text: The .cnj route computes mesh bounding spheres from the vertex positions and leaves ModelMesh.Tag null.
tokens: Mesh spheres computed from the vertex positions
concepts.note: The claim said the CNJ route leaves BoundingSphere degenerate; TARGET computes it.

concepts.section: Four model asset routes, not two
concepts.text: The .cnj route creates buffers and stock effects per described part, while a named custom effect goes through the manager's cached Load<std::shared_ptr<Effect>>, so repeated names can share one object — not XNB's shared-resource graph.

concepts.section: Four model asset routes, not two
concepts.text: Direct .gltf/.glb loading parses glTF 2.0 and its buffers in process without CNJ or sidecars and reuses the import core: sparse-safe extraction, topological skin ordering, material/image extraction, morph and animation data.

concepts.section: Four model asset routes, not two
concepts.text: Direct glTF returns one Model with the selected scene's placements including independent skin groups at unit scale 1.0; SkinsEXT keeps each skin-to-mesh mapping and Tag aliases the first skin.

concepts.section: Four model asset routes, not two
concepts.text: Direct glTF builds an identity synthetic root plus one ModelBone per reachable node, parent before child; a rigid mesh is attached to its instancing node, a skinned mesh to the root so the palette does not double-apply the node transform.

concepts.section: Four model asset routes, not two
concepts.text: Direct glTF keeps morph targets and tracks on each part's Tag, cameras in Model::CamerasEXT, a material-variant selection API, and GltfImportReportEXT counts and diagnostics.

concepts.section: Four model asset routes, not two
concepts.text: Direct glTF decodes images in memory and caches them by glTF image during one import; buffers are per primitive, while effects are shared per material, skin and import shape.
tokens: One effect per material, skin and import shape
concepts.note: The claim said effects remain per primitive; TARGET shares one effect per (material, skin, shape, UV mapping) — GLTF-238.

concepts.section: Four model asset routes, not two
concepts.text: The .skinnedmodel.json route dispatches to SkinnedModelTypeReader and produces SkinnedModelEXT via Load<std::shared_ptr<SkinnedModelEXT>>; it is neither a CNJ alias nor an old name of the Model descriptor.

concepts.section: Four model asset routes, not two
concepts.text: Loading the legacy route opts into a different public type, animation representation and draw path; its presence is a compatibility route, not evidence that the Model reader accepts another spelling.

concepts.section: Four model asset routes, not two
concepts.text: The .cnb route rebuilds a Model through the same helpers as the .cnj reader, restoring skeleton, clips, morph data and lights but not cameras, variants or the import report.
tokens: no cameras, material variants or import report

concepts.section: Four model asset routes, not two
concepts.text: Route choice: .xnb for compiled XNA fidelity, .cnb for a compiled CNA asset, .cnj for a reviewable self-contained description, direct glTF for in-process import, the legacy route only when consuming SkinnedModelEXT.
concepts.note: Adds the .cnb route that TARGET provides.

concepts.section: Four model asset routes, not two
concepts.text: Route tests do not make the routes interchangeable: only direct glTF fills cameras; only direct glTF and .cnj fill the report and variants.
concepts.note: The claim listed cameras among CNJ-tested features; the CNJ route carries no cameras at TARGET.

concepts.section: Four model asset routes, not two
concepts.text: The generated corpus and ladder cover scene graphs, skins, rigid and skeletal animation, morphs, material state and pixels; exact denominators are on the conformance page.

concepts.section: Lifetime and copies: value syntax, one mutable graph
concepts.text: Model is copy-constructible with the compiler-generated copy, which is not a deep clone: collection wrappers, Root and Tag pointers, cameras, skins and report are copied; the ownership handle and material-variant state are shared.
concepts.note: Extends the claim with TARGET's CNAEXT members: cameras/skins/report copied by value, variant state shared.

concepts.section: Lifetime and copies: value syntax, one mutable graph
concepts.text: Every bone, mesh, part, buffer and effect is the same object after a copy, so bone, part or effect mutation through one copy is visible through every copy.

concepts.section: Lifetime and copies: value syntax, one mutable graph
concepts.text: Selecting a material variant on one copy switches the shared parts for all copies.
tokens: switches the shared parts for all of them

concepts.section: Lifetime and copies: value syntax, one mutable graph
concepts.text: Each reader fills the ownership handle: XNB retains bones, meshes, parts, shared buffers, effects and tag objects; the .cnj/.cnb/glTF readers share one ModelResources bundle that also holds textures, skinning data, rigid clips and morph data.
concepts.note: XNB now also owns tag objects.

concepts.section: Lifetime and copies: value syntax, one mutable graph
concepts.text: Because the bundle is shared by every copy, Model::Tag and part Tags remain valid as long as any copy lives.
tokens: as long as any copy lives

concepts.section: Lifetime and copies: value syntax, one mutable graph
concepts.text: Two Load<Model> calls of one name return wrappers over the same graph; CopyBoneTransformsFrom through one is seen through the other, and Unload only clears the manager's cache.

concepts.section: Lifetime and copies: value syntax, one mutable graph
concepts.text: Test evidence: two loads share parts, buffers and an effect mutation and a second manager shares nothing; a copy shares buffers and outlives the original; unload/reload and 1,000 load/unload cycles; XNB loads reuse the cached vertex buffer.
concepts.note: The claim said no test copies a model and checks shared mutation or unload; TARGET's GltfPerformance suite pins these.

concepts.section: Lifetime and copies: value syntax, one mutable graph
concepts.text: Reassigning the top-level Tag changes only that wrapper's pointer; a mesh or part Tag or any bone/part/effect change is made on the shared graph.

concepts.section: Lifetime and copies: value syntax, one mutable graph
concepts.text: FNA returns its cached Model class reference so assignment aliases even the top-level wrapper; CNA's value syntax is not a deep-copy compatibility promise.

target.evidence: FNA behaviour not re-read; stated as XNA/FNA class semantics

concepts.section: Lifetime and copies: value syntax, one mutable graph
concepts.text: A caller needing two independent copies of one asset uses two ContentManagers.

concepts.section: Hand-built graphs have no automatic owner
concepts.text: The CNAEXT Model constructors store the caller's raw bone and mesh addresses, allocate nothing and install no ownership bundle; the Model constructors do not even keep the device pointer (meshes do).
tokens: do not even keep the device pointer

concepts.section: Hand-built graphs have no automatic owner
concepts.text: The four/five-argument constructor requires meshParentBones to be empty (parents stay null) or to have one entry per mesh, else std::out_of_range("meshParentBones").

concepts.section: Hand-built graphs have no automatic owner
concepts.text: The constructors are extensions because FNA creates these graph objects inside its readers rather than asking game code to manage them.
tokens: FNA creates these objects inside its readers

concepts.section: Hand-built graphs have no automatic owner
concepts.text: A hand-built model is drawable only while its whole graph and device outlive every copy; returning it after backing objects die leaves dangling pointers.

concepts.section: Hand-built graphs have no automatic owner
concepts.text: setOwnedResources(std::shared_ptr<void>) lets an owner attach one aggregate lifetime object, retaining only what it owns — not a raw device pointer, an external tag or another unowned address.

concepts.section: Hand-built graphs have no automatic owner
concepts.text: ContentManager::Unload clears the manager's asset map; it neither walks a model nor invalidates a held value, and a retained model still needs its device alive when drawing.
concepts.note: The claim said Unload clears generic asset and texture lookup maps; TARGET has no separate texture cache.

concepts.section: Hand-built graphs have no automatic owner
concepts.text: Drop every model copy before tearing down the device; cache eviction is not a safe concurrent reload or a universal resource destructor.
tokens: drop every model copy before tearing down the device

concepts.section: Skinning: two independent systems, not one
concepts.text: CNA ships separate systems for animated meshes: AnimationPlayer with SkinningData for Model, MorphTargetDataEXT for morphs, and SkinnedModelEXT for avatars; conflating them is an easy mistake.
tokens: do not share a runtime graph

concepts.section: Skinning: two independent systems, not one
concepts.text: AnimationPlayer mirrors the classes of Microsoft's unshipped XNA Skinned Model Sample, not framework code, and is CNAEXT.

concepts.section: Skinning: two independent systems, not one
concepts.text: AnimationPlayer API: StartClip(clip), Update(TimeSpan, relativeToCurrentTime, loop = true), GetBoneTransforms, GetWorldTransforms and GetSkinTransforms, the last feeding SkinnedEffect::SetBoneTransforms.

concepts.section: Skinning: two independent systems, not one
concepts.text: Skinning data (bone count, hierarchy, bind and inverse-bind pose, clips) is stashed on a loaded Model's Tag, the Skinned Model Sample's convention, because XNA's Model has no skinning property.

concepts.section: Skinning: two independent systems, not one
concepts.text: Morph targets are an independent glTF-style system: CPU re-blend and full vertex-buffer re-upload on every SetMorphWeightsEXT, a simplicity-over-throughput trade-off.

concepts.section: Skinning: two independent systems, not one
concepts.text: The morph type is MorphTargetDataEXT; MorphTargetEXT.hpp is only its header name.
concepts.note: The claim named the type MorphTargetEXT; the type is MorphTargetDataEXT.

concepts.section: Skinning: two independent systems, not one
concepts.text: glTF weights channels target a mesh-instance node, not a bone index, so morph weights have no relationship to AnimationPlayer's bone timeline.

concepts.section: Skinning: two independent systems, not one
concepts.text: Morph weights support LINEAR, STEP and real CUBICSPLINE Hermite interpolation and attach through a part's Tag.

concepts.section: Skinning: two independent systems, not one
concepts.text: SkinnedModelEXT for avatars is deliberately not built on Model/ModelBone/ModelMesh, has its own skeleton and clip binaries, and its own tests.
concepts.note: Covered in full by the avatars deep dive.

concepts.section: Skinning: two independent systems, not one
concepts.text: Keyframe and AnimationClip are aliases of KeyframeEXT and AnimationClipEXT, so the Model path and the avatar path share keyframe types and clip loading but not sampling code.

concepts.section: Driving AnimationPlayer with a test-adapted example
concepts.text: AnimationPlayerTests builds the smallest rig that exercises hierarchy composition: bone 1 child of bone 0 offset (0,1,0), bone 0's track moving it from origin to (2,0,0) over one second.

concepts.section: Driving AnimationPlayer with a test-adapted example
concepts.text: SkeletonHierarchy is a flat parent-index array with -1 meaning root, the representation glTF and most exporters use, not a pointer tree.

concepts.section: Driving AnimationPlayer with a test-adapted example
concepts.text: GetWorldTransforms gives each bone's absolute transform (useful for attachments); GetSkinTransforms is pre-multiplied by InverseBindPose, the bone's delta from bind pose that GPU skinning needs.

concepts.section: Driving AnimationPlayer with a test-adapted example
concepts.text: At half a second in the fixture, bone 0's world translation is (1,0,0) and bone 1's is (1,1,0): the child inherits the parent's motion through composition.

concepts.section: Driving AnimationPlayer with a test-adapted example
concepts.text: A Keyframe defaults rotation to identity and scale to one, so a key may carry translation only.

concepts.section: Driving AnimationPlayer with a test-adapted example
concepts.text: The player suites also pin clip start/middle/end, clamping, wrapping, relative accumulation, bind pose without a clip, inverse-bind multiplication, both refusal rules, negative-time wrap and zero-duration hold.

concepts.section: A two-target morph from the test suite
concepts.text: MorphTargetEXTTests builds every case on one stride-32 triangle with two targets: target 0 moves every vertex +1 Z without normal change, target 1 moves only vertex 0 by +2 X and tilts its normal toward +X.

concepts.section: A two-target morph from the test suite
concepts.text: Morph blending is additive: at full weight on both targets vertex 0 becomes (2,0,1) and vertex 1 (1,0,1).

concepts.section: A two-target morph from the test suite
concepts.text: BlendMorphTargetsEXT renormalizes every blended normal, because a weighted sum of unit vectors is not unit length; (0,0,1)+(1,0,0) comes back as (0.707,0,0.707).

concepts.text: Texture coordinates, blend weights and indices are copied from the base pose unchanged.

concepts.text: A weight vector whose length differs from the target count throws rather than truncating or ignoring extra entries.

concepts.section: A worked example: naming an arbitrary root bone, and how the fix was proven to work

concepts.section: Collections are read views, but not uniform ones
concepts.text: All four model collections offer XNA's enumerator (GetEnumerator/Current/MoveNext/Reset) and CNAEXT begin()/end() for range-for.
concepts.note: The claim said the collections expose C++ iteration rather than FNA's enumerators; TARGET has both (XNA-ENUM-001).

concepts.section: Collections are read views, but not uniform ones

concepts.section: The runtime hierarchy
concepts.text: Model::getBoundingSphereEXTProperty returns one sphere around every mesh at its current parent-bone placement (nullopt without meshes), recomputed from current bone transforms, shear-safe, and unioned under the current skin palette for skinned meshes.

concepts.section: The runtime hierarchy
concepts.text: The material-variant API selects by source index with -1 as default, applies model-wide, restores defaults for unmapped parts and throws std::out_of_range for invalid values.

concepts.section: The runtime hierarchy
concepts.text: ModelCameraEXT::WorldTransform is an import-time snapshot; the live camera placement is the absolute transform of the bone its SceneNodeIndex names; an infinite-far perspective uses CreateInfinitePerspectiveFieldOfViewEXT.

concepts.section: The runtime hierarchy
concepts.text: ModelMeshPart carries per-slot sampler states (five core, two specular) that are LinearWrap on non-glTF routes; the setters ignore an out-of-range slot for forward compatibility.

issues.text: ModelMesh::Draw guards Ensure3DSupported with a null-device check but then calls graphicsDevice_->SetVertexBuffer unconditionally, so a positive-count part in a mesh constructed with a null device dereferences null.

Model::Draw on a model with zero bones and a mesh effect indexes the thread-local scratch vector at 0 without growing it (empty vector or stale slot from an earlier model on the thread); operator[] is unchecked.
CopyAbsoluteBoneTransformsTo assumes parent-before-child order and does not detect cycles or misordered hand-built graphs; a documented construction invariant rather than a defect.
Only EasyGL has renderer-local Model draw/hierarchy example programs; other GPU families render Model graphs only through glTF L7 campaigns.

BlendMorphTargetsEXT indexes NormalDeltas[t] without checking the outer vector length (TangentDeltas is guarded) and indexes inner delta vectors by vertex without a length check; inconsistent hand-built MorphTargetDataEXT is undefined behaviour.
Process-wide Model::Draw scratch buffer race is absent at TARGET (thread_local, concurrency test).
Morph normals on PBR strides are blended at TARGET (canonical offsets).
